repo_standards_ref: docs/agents/CREW_CONTEXT.md, docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md, references/global-crew.md, g1-implement-handoff.md (design-it-twice explicitly skipped)

smells.finding: test_load_roundtrips_field_values (cyclomatic_complexity=22) and test_error_record_never_loses_a_failure (cyclomatic_complexity=20) in test_grip_store.py are long, flat sequences of ~14-19 field-by-field assert statements each. This is the same underlying issue already recorded as the r4-quality BLOCKER (project's own simplification_limits gate fails on these two functions, limit <20). Fowler antidote: split into a small round-trip helper (e.g. assert a dict of expected field->value pairs in a loop, or split into two focused tests: identity fields vs numeric fields) to bring both under the complexity/line limits.

GripStore's __init__/_connect/_init_schema/_migrate_missing_columns/upsert/has/load are structurally near-identical to EstimateStore's own methods (own SQLite file, PRAGMA table_info diff, INSERT OR REPLACE, WHERE-clause-from-non-None-args load). A shared lightweight base (e.g. a generic SqliteRecordStore) would remove this duplication now that two real instances exist (per global-everyone.md's own 'one adapter = hypothetical seam, two = real one' rule) -- worth a Triage candidate for a future consolidation pass, but not a defect in this gate.

override.repo_standard: g1-implement-handoff.md Constraints: 'Follow estimate_store.py's exact shape/pattern -- design-it-twice is deliberately skipped for this per issue #663 (the interface shape is precedented, not novel). Do not invent a different persistence approach.'
override.reason: The handoff explicitly forbids inventing a different (e.g. shared-base-class) persistence approach for this gate -- mirroring the precedented per-file shape exactly was the assigned task, not a lapse. Extraction is legitimate future work, not something this gate was authorized to do.

smells.finding: The (year, gp_name, session_type) triple recurs as parallel arguments across has()/load()/error_record()/_PK rather than a single key value object.

override.repo_standard: estimate_store.py's own _PK = ("year", "gp_name", "session_type", "constructor") and every method signature repeats the same clump (has/load/error_record) -- the layer's established, precedented convention this gate was directed to mirror exactly.
override.reason: Introducing a SessionKey value object here would diverge from the sibling store's own signature shape mid-layer, creating an inconsistent convention between the two stores for no gate-scoped benefit; the handoff's design-it-twice-skipped directive covers this too.

smells.finding: fit_status is a bare str with a documented-in-prose but code-unenforced enum ("ok"|"thin_fallback"|"error"); no validation rejects an out-of-set value at construction or upsert time.

override.repo_standard: estimate_store.py's EstimateRecord.fit_status is equally a bare, unvalidated str ("ok"|"error") -- the layer's existing, precedented convention.
override.reason: Matches the mirrored file's own convention exactly; adding enum validation only to the new store would be an inconsistent, gate-scoped divergence from the sibling store CREW_CONTEXT and the handoff both said to mirror, not extend. Worth a layer-wide follow-up (both stores together), not this gate alone.

smells.finding: GripEstimateRecord's ~20-field constructor is the dataclass-as-parameter-object pattern itself (mirroring EstimateRecord's own much larger field count) -- the sanctioned antidote to this smell, not an instance of it. error_record() takes 6 params, well within norms.
must_exist mirrors an already-used, real EstimateStore guard (#575 read-only-existence-guard); every field exists because g2/g3 are commissioned to consume it, not speculative.

Docstrings explain PK rationale, field-naming provenance (cumulative_track_laps_max), and the error-path convention -- genuine clarification of real design decisions, not compensating for unclear code.
